messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated DNS error-rate (NX/SERVFAIL) observed from eu-west-1 edge resolvers affecting GeoDNS lookups. Automated probes show increased latency to external authoritative providers (Cloudflare) and intermittent SERVFAILs. Pager: leo.

leo: on it. seeing the spike on dashboards — API 5xxs up ~3% for the last 3m. attaching probe summary.

cloudops: paste:```
> probe eu-west-1 -> cloudflare-a: 250ms, SERVFAIL x 12/20
> probe eu-west-1 -> route53: 40ms, OK x 20/20
> client-side resolver traces: intermittent NX from cf-ns-01
```

leo: thanks. quick triage Qs: did any recent egress/az routing change land in eu-west-1 in the last hour?

marta: no infra deploys in that window. Network team rolled a minor BGP tweak 2h ago but it was global and verified. I'll pull VPC egress tables.

kevin: I'm seeing an odd pattern — requests from our eu-west-1 LB are getting answers from Cloudflare that are inconsistent vs Route53; looks like selective authoritative path degradation. Could be CF peering flap.

oncall-bot: Paging escalation: leo -> marta (primary network), kevin (dns), cloudops (ops). ETA for follow-up: 5m.

marta: confirmed: one AZ (eu-west-1b) shows asymmetric egress via a transit peer that is reporting packet-loss to Cloudflare POPs. Not all AZs impacted.

leo: customer impact: hosted inference control-plane name resolution failures cause model fetch failures -> 503s for some requests. Early estimate: 20k requests/min, ~3% error amplification for eu region; about 27 customer tokens with >1% errors.

kevin: mitigation plan option A (fast): adjust GeoDNS routing to avoid Cloudflare as authoritative for eu-west-1 for the next 15m and route queries to Route53-only path. Option B (network): force egress through alternate transit (requires AZ routing change). A is lower risk and faster. Thoughts?

marta: agree A first. I can update GeoDNS policy to prefer route53 endpoints for eu-west traffic and lower TTL to 30s to accelerate rollouts. Doing TTL change now has propagation caveats but should take effect for our resolvers quickly.

cloudops: I'm enabling a temporary resolver fallback on edge boxes to prefer 1.1.1.1/9.9.9.9 for domains that hit CF NS. Will push a small config via SSM to eu-west LBs.

leo: go for A + resolver fallback. Keep network reroute as fallback if this doesn't stabilize in 10m.

kevin: executing GeoDNS change:```
# geo policy patch
set policy eu-west prefer: route53
set ttl 30
```
Applying now.

oncall-bot: Action logged: geo-dns policy updated by kevin at 5790001335.

cloudops: SSM push to edge resolvers started. snippet:```
commands:
  - sed -i 's/^nameserver.*/nameserver 1.1.1.1/' /etc/resolv.conf
  - service dnsmasq restart || systemctl restart systemd-resolved
```

marta: also throttling BGP session reset to that transit peer in eu-west-1b to avoid flap reinjection. I'm coordinating with provider.

leo: monitoring... dashboards show NX/SERVFAIL down by ~70% in the last 3m. HTTP 5xxs down to baseline +0.5%. Good signal.

kevin: still seeing a handful of clients with stale CF NS cached answers. Recommended communications: short status update explaining partial DNS degradation, note mitigation (GeoDNS fallback to Route53 + resolver fallback) and that we're monitoring. Also recommend advising on-prem / private deploy customers: add alternate resolvers or pin to route53 resolver endpoints as a workaround.

status-bot: DRAFT status: [Investigating] Intermittent DNS errors in eu-west-1 causing some API 5xxs. Mitigation: GeoDNS temporarily routing eu queries to Route53 and edge resolvers configured to fall back to public resolvers.

leo: +1. post it, include ETA for next update in 30m.

marta: provider reports partial packet loss on transit peer; they are throttling flows and rerouting. They suggest full fix in ~90m.

cloudops: rolling rollback plan if GeoDNS change causes unexpected traffic shift: revert policy and reapply original bindings. Revert command ready:```
set policy eu-west restore original
set ttl 300
```

leo: good to have revert. Keep this thread for handoff. I'm going offline in 20m; marta please take primary oncall in next handoff. kevin, continue to monitor authoritative answer consistency.

marta: acknowledged. I'll take post-incident follow-ups and coordinate provider write-up.

leo: final note for postmortem: track root cause — transit peer instability causing asymmetric reachability to Cloudflare POPs -> inconsistent authoritative answers -> GeoDNS/edge resolver cache divergences -> client 5xx amplification. Action items: 1) formalize auto-fallback policy for GeoDNS when third-party NS latency rises, 2) add resolver diversity checks to health probes, 3) run tabletop with network provider.

status-bot: Update posted. Next update scheduled +30m.

kevin: thanks team. closing slack loop once metrics stable for 15m. :thumbsup:
